facts.raw_span: multiple (approximately 10) bluish, partially keratotic papules and nodules on the lower legs
The lesions had been growing very slowly in number and size since age 24
had been bleeding occasionally after trauma
right-sided hemiparesis and hemianopsia caused by an intracranial hemorrhage
recurrent seizures at age 4
lipolymphedema of the lower legs attributed to functional venous insufficiency with insufficient venous pump activity
had been wearing compression stockings for years
similar conditions in the patient's father and aunt, with the father having died of an intracranial hemorrhage in his early 70s
Sonography: Demonstrated intradermal slow-flow vascular malformations with a maximum diameter of 1.2 cm

Biopsy revealed a well-circumscribed lesion with hyperkeratosis and acanthosis of the epidermis overlying a conglomerate of dilated venous-like malformations with continuous smooth muscle in the upper dermis, partly showing thrombosis
Detection of a heterozygous pathogenic KRIT1 variant

concepts.why: The patient's history of intracranial hemorrhage, sonography demonstrating intradermal slow-flow vascular malformations, and biopsy revealing dilated venous-like malformations with thrombosis, along with the detection of a heterozygous pathogenic KRIT1 variant, support this diagnosis.

The patient's multiple bluish, partially keratotic papules and nodules on the lower legs, lipolymphedema, and history of bleeding after trauma, along with sonography and biopsy findings, are consistent with this diagnosis.

The patient's lipolymphedema, multiple bluish papules and nodules, and sonography findings are consistent with this diagnosis, although the absence of other characteristic features, such as port-wine stains, makes it less likely.

rationales.F01: Multiple bluish papules and nodules are consistent with blue rubber bleb nevus syndrome.
rationales.F03: Bleeding after trauma is a feature that can be seen in blue rubber bleb nevus syndrome.
rationales.F04: Intracranial hemorrhage is a known complication of cerebral cavernous malformations.
rationales.F05: Recurrent seizures can be associated with cerebral cavernous malformations.
rationales.F06: Lipolymphedema can be seen in Klippel-Trenaunay syndrome.
rationales.F08: Family history of similar conditions and intracranial hemorrhage suggests a hereditary component, consistent with cerebral cavernous malformations.
rationales.F09: Intradermal slow-flow vascular malformations can be seen in blue rubber bleb nevus syndrome.
rationales.F10: Histopathology showing dilated venous-like malformations is consistent with blue rubber bleb nevus syndrome.
rationales.F11: Detection of a heterozygous pathogenic KRIT1 variant is diagnostic for cerebral cavernous malformations.

frontier_selector.rationale: Detection of a heterozygous pathogenic KRIT1 variant and presence of intracranial hemorrhage support Cerebral cavernous malformation as the most specific diagnosis.
